chunks: And Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:
"There is no salat (prayer) except toward the qiblah."
He said: I said, "And where is the boundary of the qiblah?" He said: "What is between the east and the west is all qiblah."
He said: I said, "Then whoever prays facing other than the qiblah, or on a cloudy day at other than the time?" He said: "He repeats."

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the qiblah, the direction required for salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: the east, used here to define one side of the directional range
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the west, used here to define the other side of the directional range
key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: the appointed time, meaning the proper time for salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَدُّ: boundary or limit, referring to the extent of the qiblah direction
key_terms.صَلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.غَيْمٍ: cloudiness or a cloudy day, mentioned as a circumstance of error
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats, indicating the obligation to perform the salat (prayer) again

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in the wrong direction or at the wrong time according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that salat (prayer) must be performed toward the qiblah and explains the recognized directional scope of the qiblah. It also gives a legal ruling that one who prays facing other than the qiblah, or prays outside the proper time due to error on a cloudy day, must repeat the prayer.
